pass_a_gloss: For it is permitted both to eat meats and to drink wine, but not wholly without loss [is] the authority in these things. But also the holding back [is] useful, so that, not thickening the flesh with the luxuries, we may not make savage against ourselves the passions in it. If then we hold back from those things because of ourselves, much more because of the brother; so that he may not strike against [them], because of what has been said: You will love your neighbour as yourself. Therefore take one another to yourselves, just as Christ also took you to himself, into glory of God. One body we are, the many, and members of one another, according to what has been written, Christ stringing us together into oneness by the bonds of the love: for he himself [is] the one who made the both one, and loosed the middle wall of the fence, having made idle the law of the commandments in decrees. It is needful, then, indeed, to think the same toward one another, and if one member suffers anything, that all the members suffer with [it]; or if one member is glorified, that all the members rejoice. pass_b_english: For it is lawful to eat meat and to drink wine, but freedom in these things is not altogether without harm (Romans 14:21). Abstaining is also useful, so that we do not fatten the flesh with soft living and make the passions within it rage wild against ourselves. If, then, we abstain from these things for our own sake, much more for our brother’s, so that he may not stumble, because of the saying, “You shall love your neighbour as yourself” (Leviticus 19:18).

“Therefore receive one another, as Christ also received you, for the glory of God” (Romans 15:7). We who are many are one body, and members of one another, as it is written (Romans 12:5), since Christ binds us together into unity with the bonds of love: “For He Himself is the one who made both one and broke down the dividing wall of partition, abolishing the law of commandments in ordinances” (Ephesians 2:14–15). So we must be of the same mind toward one another (Romans 12:16); and if one member suffers, all the members must suffer with it, and if one member is honoured, all the members must rejoice (1 Corinthians 12:26). That is why he says, “Receive one another, as Christ also received you, for the glory of God.” And we shall receive one another if we choose to be of the same mind, bear one another’s burdens (Galatians 6:2), and keep “the unity of the…”

revisions.summary: Pass A, lemmas, choices and bible_refs rebuilt from the Greek to match the reviewed English; pass_b_english is the current English.

review_notes: Book row had wrong sense in several clauses: ἀζήμιον ('without harm') rendered 'without restriction'; παχύνοντες ('fattening') rendered 'harden'; καθ' ἑαυτῶν ('against ourselves') dropped; δι' ἑαυτούς ('for our own sake') rendered 'for their own sake'; the brother's stumbling wrongly made to come from the commandment; ὑμᾶς ('you') in Romans 15:7 rendered 'us' and 'into the glory'; the repeated lemma and the closing clause (bearing one another's burdens, Galatians 6:2, keeping the unity…) omitted, with a stray fragment 'Unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace' left as a paragraph although that phrase belongs to u11-rem-mid. No inline citations. Retranslated clause by clause with citations; page number 247 dropped; the Ephesians 4:3 quotation is left open with an ellipsis to join the staged u11-rem-mid. The book row's translator_notes are also wrong ('abolishing in dogmas is a textual variant', 'the middle of the wall') and should be replaced when this fix is applied.
Page number 247 is edition apparatus and is omitted.
Ends inside the quotation of Ephesians 4:3, which continues at the start of u11-rem-mid.
